Build the per-cell corpus statistics

Source: R/md-stats.R
md_build_stats.Rd

Corpus statistics depend on which rows a spec selects (PLAN.md section 6a), so they cannot be one number per name. They can be one number per cell, where a cell is layer x variant_class x corroboration band: every spec without a cross-cutting filter is a union of cells, and its statistics are the exact sum of its cells' (section 6c).

Usage

md_build_stats(con = NULL)

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

Value

Row counts of the three tables, invisibly.

Details

Counted over name_compact rows, one per (ein, name_key). Each such row is in exactly one cell - one layer per EIN, one variant class per row - so the sums are exact for EIN counts too, not just row counts.

stat_cell

layer, variant_class, band, n_rows

stat_name_cell

layer, variant_class, band, name_key, n_eins: EINs holding the name in that cell

stat_token_cell

layer, variant_class, band, token, n_rows: name rows containing the token, by npnormalize::np_token_idf()'s rules - split on space, unique per name, at least two characters, no stopwords

Name rows, not frame rows

npmatch's own npnormalize::np_name_freq() and npnormalize::np_token_idf() count rows of the compiled frame, where a name is repeated once per paired address. These cells count names, so an EIN with three addresses counts once. The difference is real and md_compile() reports both.
